subject: SLO signoff checklist & telemetry handover for onboarding
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Evan Ross <evan.ross@kilnretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLO signoff checklist & telemetry handover for onboarding

Hi Evan / Sofia,

Thanks again for choosing Redwood — excited to get Kiln Retail across the finish line. To make the onboarding benchmark run crisp and signable I put together a short SLO checklist + proposed telemetry handover plan. Goal is to run a single acceptance window and gather artifacts you can use for your internal compliance and SRE signoff.

Proposed acceptance targets (customer-provided workloads):
- P95 generation latency <= 200 ms
- P99 tail latency <= 400 ms
- Sustained throughput target: 1,200 req/s for 30m (peak ramps to 1,800 req/s for 5m)
- Error rate <= 0.1% (5xx / total requests)

Planned test structure:
1) Smoke (5m) — validate traffic, keys, telemetry ingestion
2) Ramp (10m) — linear ramp to 50% of throughput
3) Steady-state (30m) — sustained throughput window with representative prompt mix
4) Spike test (5–10m) — short ramp to peak

Telemetry & artifacts we will share:
- Raw loadtest CSV (requests, latencies, status codes) [attachment]
- Grafana dashboards link for the run
- p95/p99 time-series PNGs [attachment]
- Runbook with exact request payloads and seed corpus (Drive link)

Dependencies we need from Kiln before the run:
- Test API key (scoped) and a single test workspace or tenant to isolate traffic
- Representative sample of your prompt mix (200–500 examples)
- Preferred test window (timezone & date)

Can you confirm availability for a 2h window next week? Suggested windows: Thu 16 Sep 10:00–12:00 PT or Fri 17 Sep 09:00–11:00 PT. If those don't work, propose two alternatives.

I'll loop in Monica for telemetry and Ben to own the actual execution.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: runbook-v1.2.pdf (pdf)]
From: Evan Ross <evan.ross@kilnretail.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@kilnretail.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO signoff checklist & telemetry handover for onboarding

Thanks Marcus — this looks good and very actionable. Quick clarifications before we lock the window:
- Our workload includes both streaming responses and regular generation. For streaming requests the P95 target can be evaluated on final token emission; is that how you want to measure it?
- Do you need us to white-list any IPs or provide an allowlist for the test traffic?

We can do Thu 16 Sep 10:00–12:00 PT. I'll provide the test API key and a 300-example prompt sample by EOD today.

Sofia will be on the call on Thursday.

—Evan
Evan Ross
VP Engineering, Kiln Retail
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 12:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Kiln runbook & resource booking (Thu 16 Sep 10:00–12:00 PT)

Ben / Monica — heads up: Kiln confirmed Thu 16 Sep 10–12 PT. Evan will provide API key + prompt set tonight. Please reserve the following:
- Dedicated nodes: 4 x A100 (dedicated pool) for the 30m steady-state and spike windows
- Grafana snapshot and retention setting to persist the run for 30 days
- Network: confirm no outbound allowlist is needed; they'll provide keys but we should still whitelist our test-range where possible

Ben: you'll run the load script from runbook-v1.2.pdf (Drive link below). Make sure batching profile is the default first pass (batch_size=8) — we may tune to hit the 1,200 req/s target without increasing latency. If p95 drifts above 200ms in steady-state, try batch_size=4 and enable KV prefix caching for the prompt set.

Drive / Tickets:
- Runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcExampleLinkRunbook
- HubSpot: hs_record_7891023 (onboarding ticket)

I'll be on the call to coordinate; Monica will own telemetry and artifact drop.

-Marcus
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Evan Ross <evan.ross@kilnretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Load run results (Kiln) — initial readout

Attaching the raw CSV and quick graphs from today’s run. High level summary below.

Summary:
- Run window: 2026-09-16 10:05–10:50 PT (steady-state 30m)
- Config used: 4 x A100, model: redwood-rlm-13b-quant, batch_size=8, prefix caching: off (default)
- Observed throughput: sustained 1,150 req/s (slight under target)
- P95 latency: 215 ms (10% over target)
- P99 latency: 380 ms (within target)
- Error rate: 0.06% (OK)

Notes & next steps:
- The p95 drift is concentrated on the first 8 minutes of steady-state when longer prompts (95th percentile prompt length) were exercised. After minute 8 we saw better stability.
- Actionable fixes: reduce batch_size to 4 + enable KV prefix caching for the 300-example corpus — simulation shows this should push p95 down ~30 ms and increase sustain throughput to ~1,250 req/s.
- Attached artifacts: loadtest-results-20260916.csv, p95-p99-latency-graphs.png

Evan — if you’re comfortable with the mitigation, we can run a quick follow-up 15m validation tomorrow morning (Fri 17 Sep 09:00–09:30 PT). If that passes we’ll produce the final signoff package (graphs + runbook + raw CSV + Grafana link).

[Attachment: loadtest-results-20260916.csv (csv)]
[Attachment: p95-p99-latency-graphs.png (png)]

—Ben
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Evan Ross <evan.ross@kilnretail.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@kilnretail.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Load run results (Kiln) — initial readout

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear readout and proposed fix. We’re happy to proceed with the mitigation (batch_size=4 + prefix caching) and confirm the follow-up window tomorrow 09:00–09:30 PT. If that run meets the p95 <= 200ms target we’ll consider this accepted for the onboarding acceptance criteria.

We’d also like the final artifact bundle (CSV, PNGs, runbook with exact commands, Grafana snapshot) added to our shared drive folder and a short one-page signoff note we can attach to our internal change request.

Sofia will join the validation run and help verify sample prompts.

Best,
Evan

> Running follow-up now with batch_size=4 and prefix caching enabled.
> Preliminary numbers: p95 at 186 ms, sustained throughput ~1,260 req/s.
